docs.title: medhira-rn-expo-json-ui-engine
docs.text:
Engineering Intelligence Across Everything

A JSON-driven UI engine for React Native and Expo that enables dynamic, runtime-rendered interfaces without rebuilding the app.

Note

This package is designed specifically for Expo React Native projects only, and requires Expo SDK version 52 or higher.

docs.title: Why MEDHIRA?
docs.text:
In today's mobile app landscape, many applications—especially those powered by chatbots or backend-driven platforms—require the flexibility to render UIs dynamically from a backend source. MEDHIRA JSON UI Engine enables exactly that:

  • Backend-Driven UIs - Perfect for chatbot-driven layouts and CMS integrations
  • Runtime Rendering - Render components via JSON without code changes or app rebuilds
  • Performance Optimized - Built with performance in mind using style caching
  • Flexible & Extensible - Component registry and custom type support

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• :material-render: Render UI directly from JSON
  • :material-puzzle: Reusable component registry via useComponent
  • :material-update: Runtime support for static JSON, functions, and RxJS-like observables
  • :material-react: Built-in support for 25+ React Native/Expo components
  • :material-eye-show: Conditional visibility with showIf
  • :material-cog: Style optimization with caching
  • :material-language-typescript: Full TypeScript support

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
import { JSONUI } from 'medhira-rn-expo-json-ui-engine';

const json = {
  type: 'Text',
  value: 'Hello MEDHIRA!',
  props: {
    style: { fontSize: 24 }
  }
};

export default function App() {
  return <JSONUI json={json} />;
}

docs.title: BaseUIComponent
docs.text:
interface BaseUIComponent {
  type: UITypes;
  showIf?: boolean | ((context: any) => boolean);
}

docs.title: ViewContainerComponent
docs.text:
interface ViewContainerComponent extends BaseWrapperComponent {
  type: ContainerTypes.ViewContainer;
  properties: UIComponent[];
}

docs.title: ListContainerComponent
docs.text:
interface ListContainerComponent extends BaseUIComponent {
  type: ContainerTypes.ListContainer;
  props?: UIFlashListProps;
  components?: {
    headerComponent?: UIComponent;
    footerComponent?: UIComponent;
    emptyComponent?: UIComponent;
    itemSeparatorComponent?: UIComponent;
    cellRendererComponent?: UIComponent;
    stickyHeaderComponent?: UIComponent;
  };
}

  ref: TRef;
  props?: TProps;
  properties?: UIComponent[];
}

docs.title: JSONUI Component
docs.text: The main component for rendering JSON-defined UIs.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: import { JSONUI } from 'medhira-rn-expo-json-ui-engine';

docs.title: json
docs.text:
Static JSON component definition.

<JSONUI json={myComponent} />

Type: UIComponent | UIComponent[]

docs.title: jsonSource
docs.text:
Dynamic source for the UI - can be a function or observable.

// Function
<JSONUI jsonSource={() => fetchConfig()} />

// Observable
<JSONUI jsonSource={observable$} />

// Lazy function
<JSONUI jsonSource={myLazyJson} />

Type: JSONSource

type JSONSource =
  | UIComponent
  | UIComponent[]
  | (() => UIComponent | UIComponent[])
  | { subscribe: (cb: (val: any) => void) => { unsubscribe: () => void } };

docs.title: Static JSON
docs.text:
const myUI = {
  type: 'Text',
  value: 'Hello!'
};

<JSONUI json={myUI} />

docs.title: Array of Components
docs.text:
const components = [
  { type: 'Text', value: 'Item 1' },
  { type: 'Text', value: 'Item 2' }
];

<JSONUI json={components} />

docs.title: Dynamic Source
docs.text:
<JSONUI jsonSource={() => {
  // Return component or array
  return fetch('/api/ui').then(r => r.json());
}} />

docs.title: Observable Pattern
docs.text:
import { BehaviorSubject } from 'rxjs';

const config$ = new BehaviorSubject(defaultConfig);

function App() {
  // Update will trigger re-render
  const updateConfig = (newConfig) => {
    config$.next(newConfig);
  };

  return <JSONUI jsonSource={config$} />;
}

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always provide fallback - Use default UI when loading
  2. Handle errors - Wrap in error boundaries
  3. Memoize complex JSON - Use useMemo for expensive calculations

docs.text: • API Reference

docs.title: Component Registry
docs.text: Create reusable components with the MEDHIRA component registry.

docs.title: Why Use Component Registry?
docs.text: The registry allows you to: - Define components once, use them anywhere - Parameterize components with placeholders - Build component libraries for your apps

docs.title: Creating a UseComponent
docs.text:
Use defineUseComponent to create reusable components:

import { defineUseComponent } from 'medhira-rn-expo-json-ui-engine';

const UserCard = defineUseComponent(
  'UserCard',                          // Unique reference
  { name: 'John', email: 'john@test.com' },  // Default props
  {
    type: 'ViewContainer',
    wrapperComponent: 'View',
    props: { style: { padding: 16, borderRadius: 8 } },
    properties: [
      {
        type: 'Text',
        value: '{{name}}',
        props: { style: { fontSize: 18, fontWeight: 'bold' } }
      },
      {
        type: 'Text',
        value: '{{email}}',
        props: { style: { color: 'gray' } }
      }
    ]
  }
);

docs.title: Using Placeholders
docs.text:
Use {{propName}} syntax to inject dynamic values:

const ProductCard = defineUseComponent(
  'ProductCard',
  { title: 'Product', price: 0 },
  {
    type: 'ViewContainer',
    wrapperComponent: 'View',
    properties: [
      {
        type: 'Text',
        value: '{{title}}'
      },
      {
        type: 'Text',
        value: '${{price}}'
      }
    ]
  }
);

docs.title: Using Registered Components
docs.text:
Reference components using the useComponent type:

const page = {
  type: 'ViewContainer',
  properties: [
    {
      type: 'useComponent',
      ref: 'UserCard',
      props: { name: 'Jane', email: 'jane@example.com' }
    },
    {
      type: 'useComponent',
      ref: 'ProductCard',
      props: { title: 'Premium Plan', price: 99 }
    }
  ]
};

docs.title: Advanced: Nested Placeholders
docs.text:
Placeholders work in any property:

const DynamicButton = defineUseComponent(
  'DynamicButton',
  { label: 'Click', onPress: () => {} },
  {
    type: 'Button',
    props: {
      title: '{{label}}',
      onPress: '{{onPress}}',
      style: { backgroundColor: '#007AFF' }
    }
  }
);

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use descriptive refs - 'UserCard' not 'uc'
  2. Provide defaults - Always set default props
  3. Single responsibility - One component, one purpose
  4. Document props - Comment expected prop values

docs.title: Conditional Rendering
docs.text: Show or hide components based on conditions.

docs.title: Basic Boolean
docs.text:
Use showIf with a boolean value:

const adminOnly = {
  type: 'Text',
  value: 'Admin Panel',
  showIf: true  // Always shows
};

const hidden = {
  type: 'Text',
  value: 'Hidden',
  showIf: false  // Never shows
};

docs.title: Function Condition
docs.text:
Use a function for dynamic conditions:

const context = { user: { role: 'admin' } };

const adminUI = {
  type: 'Button',
  props: { title: 'Delete All' },
  showIf: (ctx) => ctx.user?.role === 'admin'
};

docs.title: Role-Based UI
docs.text:
const menuConfig = {
  type: 'ViewContainer',
  properties: [
    {
      type: 'Text',
      value: 'Dashboard',
      showIf: true
    },
    {
      type: 'Text',
      value: 'Admin Settings',
      showIf: (ctx) => ctx.user?.role === 'admin'
    },
    {
      type: 'Button',
      props: { title: 'Logout' },
      showIf: true
    }
  ]
};

docs.title: Feature Flags
docs.text:
const newFeatureUI = {
  type: 'Button',
  props: { title: 'New Feature' },
  showIf: (ctx) => ctx.featureFlags?.newDashboard === true
};

docs.title: Loading States
docs.text:
const content = {
  type: 'ViewContainer',
  properties: [
    {
      type: 'Text',
      value: 'Loading...',
      showIf: (ctx) => ctx.loading
    },
    {
      type: 'Text',
      value: 'Content Loaded!',
      showIf: (ctx) => !ctx.loading
    }
  ]
};

docs.title: Context Pattern
docs.text:
Pass context to evaluate conditions:

const appContext = {
  user: { id: 1, role: 'admin' },
  featureFlags: { newDashboard: true },
  loading: false
};

// Pass context through your app's state management

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Keep functions simple - Complex logic in utils
  2. Use consistent context - Same structure across your app
  3. Null checks - Handle undefined properties safely

docs.title: Dynamic Sources
docs.text: Load JSON from various sources at runtime.

docs.title: Static JSON
docs.text:
The simplest approach - pass JSON directly:

<JSONUI json={myJson} />

docs.title: Function-Based Sources
docs.text:
Load JSON from a function:

const fetchConfig = async () => {
  const response = await fetch('/api/ui-config');
  return response.json();
};

<JSONUI jsonSource={fetchConfig} />

docs.title: Observable Sources
docs.text:
Use RxJS-like observables for reactive updates:

import { BehaviorSubject } from 'rxjs';

const uiSubject$ = new BehaviorSubject(defaultConfig);

<JSONUI jsonSource={uiSubject$} />

docs.title: Updating Observable Data
docs.text:
Update the UI by emitting new values:

// In your app
uiSubject$.next(newConfig);

// The UI automatically re-renders

docs.title: Observable Interface
docs.text:
The observable must implement this interface:

interface Observable {
  subscribe: (callback: (value: any) => void) => {
    unsubscribe: () => void;
  };
}

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Source Type Use Case Pros Cons Static JSON Hardcoded UIs Simple, no runtime Must rebuild app Function API-loaded UIs Dynamic, no rebuild Network needed Observable Real-time UIs Reactive updates More complex

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Caching - Cache API responses to reduce network calls
  2. Error handling - Handle loading and error states
  3. Fallback - Provide default UI when loading

docs.title: Example: Loading States
docs.text:
const [json, setJson] = useState(defaultConfig);
const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);

const loadConfig = async () => {
  setLoading(true);
  try {
    const config = await fetch('/api/ui').then(r => r.json());
    setJson(config);
  } catch (e) {
    console.error('Failed to load:', e);
  } finally {
    setLoading(false);
  }
};

<JSONUI json={loading ? loadingJson : json} />

docs.title: JSON UI Basics
docs.text: Learn how MEDHIRA renders UI from JSON definitions.

docs.title: Core Architecture
docs.text:
MEDHIRA follows a simple architecture:

  1. JSON Definition - You describe your UI as JSON
  2. JSONUI Component - The engine parses and renders the UI
  3. Runtime Updates - UI updates automatically when JSON changes

docs.title: JSON Structure
docs.text:
Every UI component has this basic structure:

{
  "type": "ComponentType",
  "showIf": true,
  "props": { ... },
  "properties": [ ... ]
}
Property Type Description type string The type of component to render showIf boolean | function Conditional visibility props object Component props passed to React Native properties array Child components (for containers)

docs.title: Leaf Components
docs.text:
Leaf components are atomic UI elements:

{
  "type": "Text",
  "value": "Hello World"
}

{
  "type": "Button",
  "props": { "title": "Click Me" }
}

docs.title: Container Components
docs.text:
Containers hold and render child components:

{
  "type": "ViewContainer",
  "wrapperComponent": "View",
  "properties": [
    { "type": "Text", "value": "Child 1" },
    { "type": "Text", "value": "Child 2" }
  ]
}

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
const dashboard = {
  type: 'ViewContainer',
  wrapperComponent: 'View',
  props: { style: { flex: 1, padding: 16 } },
  properties: [
    {
      type: 'Text',
      value: 'My Dashboard',
      props: { style: { fontSize: 32, fontWeight: 'bold' } }
    },
    {
      type: 'ViewContainer',
      wrapperComponent: 'TouchableOpacity',
      props: { style: { marginTop: 20 } },
      properties: [
        {
          type: 'Text',
          value: 'Tap to refresh',
          props: { style: { color: 'blue' } }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
};

      { type: 'Text', value: '{{description}}', props: { marginTop: 4 } }

);

const ActionCard = defineUseComponent(

  { title: '', actionLabel: 'Click' },
  {
    type: 'ViewContainer',
    wrapperComponent: 'TouchableOpacity',

    properties: [
      { type: 'Text', value: '{{title}}', props: { color: '#fff' } },
      { type: 'Button', props: { title: '{{actionLabel}}' } }
    ]
  }
);

docs.title: Real-Time Updates
docs.text:
import { BehaviorSubject } from 'rxjs';

const notificationCount$ = new BehaviorSubject(0);

// In your UI
const notificationBadge = {
  type: 'ViewContainer',
  properties: [
    { type: 'Text', value: 'Notifications' },
    // This will update automatically when observable emits
  ]
};

// Update from anywhere in your app
notificationCount$.next(5);

docs.title: Role-Based Dashboard
docs.text:
const createDashboard = (userRole: string) => ({
  type: 'ViewContainer',
  properties: [
    // Visible to all
    { type: 'Text', value: 'Welcome', showIf: true },

    // Admin only
    {
      type: 'Button',
      props: { title: 'Admin Settings' },
      showIf: userRole === 'admin'
    },

    // Manager and above
    {
      type: 'Button',
      props: { title: 'Reports' },
      showIf: userRole === 'manager' || userRole === 'admin'
    },

    // Logout for everyone
    { type: 'Button', props: { title: 'Logout' } }
  ]
});

docs.title: Memoized JSON
docs.text:
import { useMemo } from 'react';

function App() {
  const uiConfig = useMemo(() => ({
    type: 'ViewContainer',
    properties: dynamicData.map(item => ({
      type: 'Text',
      value: item.label
    }))
  }), [dynamicData]);

  return <JSONUI json={uiConfig} />;
}

docs.title: Error Boundary Pattern
docs.text:
const safeRender = (component) => {
  try {
    return renderUIComponent(component);
  } catch (error) {
    return {
      type: 'Text',
      value: 'Error rendering component',
      props: { style: { color: 'red' } }
    };
  }
};

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This guide will help you install MEDHIRA JSON UI Engine in your React Native/Expo project.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• React Native 0.81+
  • Expo SDK 52+
  • Node.js 18+

docs.title: Install the Package
docs.text:
npm install medhira-rn-expo-json-ui-engine
# or
yarn add medhira-rn-expo-json-ui-engine

docs.title: Peer Dependencies
docs.text:
This package requires the following peer dependencies. Make sure they're installed:

npm install react react-native expo react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler
# or
yarn add react react-native expo react-native-reanimated react-native-gesture-handler

docs.title: Additional Expo Packages
docs.text:
Depending on the components you use, you may need additional Expo packages:

npx expo install expo-image expo-camera expo-video expo-blur expo-linear-gradient expo-checkbox expo-status-bar expo-gl expo-live-photo

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
To verify the installation was successful, run:

import { JSONUI } from 'medhira-rn-expo-json-ui-engine';

// Basic test
const testJson = {
  type: 'Text',
  value: 'MEDHIRA is working!',
};

export default function App() {
  return <JSONUI json={testJson} />;
}

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get started with MEDHIRA JSON UI Engine in under 5 minutes.

docs.title: Your First JSON UI
docs.text:
Create a simple UI component using JSON:

import { JSONUI } from 'medhira-rn-expo-json-ui-engine';

const simpleUI = {
  type: 'ViewContainer',
  wrapperComponent: 'View',
  props: { style: { padding: 20 } },
  properties: [
    {
      type: 'Text',
      value: 'Hello, MEDHIRA!',
      props: { style: { fontSize: 24, fontWeight: 'bold' } }
    }
  ]
};

export default function App() {
  return <JSONUI json={simpleUI} />;
}

docs.title: Rendering Multiple Components
docs.text:
Build more complex UIs with nested components:

const loginForm = {
  type: 'ViewContainer',
  wrapperComponent: 'View',
  props: { style: { padding: 20 } },
  properties: [
    {
      type: 'Text',
      value: 'Welcome Back',
      props: { style: { fontSize: 28, fontWeight: 'bold', marginBottom: 20 } }
    },
    {
      type: 'TextInput',
      props: {
        placeholder: 'Email',
        style: { borderWidth: 1, padding: 10, marginBottom: 10 }
      }
    },
    {
      type: 'TextInput',
      props: {
        placeholder: 'Password',
        secureTextEntry: true,
        style: { borderWidth: 1, padding: 10, marginBottom: 20 }
      }
    },
    {
      type: 'Button',
      props: {
        title: 'Login',
        onPress: () => console.log('Login pressed')
      }
    }
  ]
};

docs.title: Using Dynamic Sources
docs.text:
Load JSON from a function or observable:

// Function-based source
<JSONUI jsonSource={() => fetchMyJson()} />

// Observable source (RxJS-like)
<JSONUI jsonSource={myObservable$} />
